what: A bench driver that fires random legal and illegal actions through the engine and proves replay-equals-state and the world invariants after each, and a browser player that drives the bench page toward an instruction by reading it as text and asking Jev one yes/no per candidate control, with a language model only for the target and the words, every loop shown, every history recorded as the corpus, and a labelled-control test for every strata page.
why: The engine's parts are a projection kept current by reducers, and nothing today proves that projection matches the log on sequences nobody wrote; the mind blocks are calibrated on labelled moments, which need coherent histories at volume no person will type; and strata is web-based, so a driver that works the page as a person does is the harness every later panel is driven by, whose mechanics the operator wants to watch. The blind walk showed the player letting an offer lapse while its accept waited, so multi-step actions are served as pending states the engine derives and the player resolves before the clock kills them. Design: docs/work/bench-driver/design.md

criteria.given: the committed world, tick length 10 and seed 7
criteria.when: bun run src/driver/main.ts --seed 7 --actions 400 --tick-minutes 10 runs with a step every 5 actions
criteria.then: it exits 0 printing a JSON report with seed 7, actions 400, steps 80, a tally holding at least one recorded event of every subkind in the registry, at least one refusal of every code in the closed set and at least one invalid action, and 480 replay checks and 480 invariant checks passed; the same seed run twice prints the same tally

mutations.change: make the engine's apply loop write only the rows whose thing is the event's actor; the C1 run must go red with a replay difference naming the thing, the part, the event and both values
make the location reducer ignore physical.arrive; the C1 run must go red with the location invariant naming the person left in transit with no arrive due
make act() record the rule's events even when the rule refused; the C1 run must go red with the refusal check naming the event count that changed
make redact() keep narrowed fields for non-participants, leaving the registry intact; the C1 run must go red with the redaction invariant naming the non-participant copy that carries words

criteria.then: project returns rows equal to values derived by hand (Glitch located in the Back Room, the item's holder moved, the offer cleared, the schedule empty), and compare returns the one difference naming the item, the holder part and both values, and null for identical rows

criteria.when: check runs over them, and separately over the freshly booted committed world
criteria.then: the first returns four violations typed holder, location, redaction and log, each naming its thing, and the second returns none

outOfScope.summary: The blind goal set and its score come after the merge, as a walk: a blind set that exists while the rule is written is not blind, so the worktree proves scoring on the calibration set and the blind score runs once the rule is on main.

frequency.reason: no blind set can exist before the rule is on main: the rule's author is the builder, and the set is written against the merged rule by another agent

outOfScope.summary: The player's text is one model-written line per run, when the target needs words; there is no voice and no persona, so the corpus carries plain lines until the block that speaks.

frequency.reason: nothing speaks in a voice in this block: voice prose is the speaking block's layer, as world-bench's design records

outOfScope.summary: The driver's actions are drawn from a biased uniform grammar with no coverage feedback; it finds what random reaches, not what a search would.

frequency.reason: the block's paths are a closed set, ten subkinds and eight refusal codes, and the driver criterion requires each to appear in one seeded run's tally

outOfScope.summary: Jev and the model are not deterministic, so a player run is not reproducible from its parameters; the corpus is committed because the run cannot be re-made.

frequency.command: recomputed from reverie/docs/work/npc-mind-frame/evidence/jev_round5_results.json: moments whose pre-registered verdict differed across the three reps

outOfScope.summary: The replay oracle cannot catch a wrong reducer, since live and replay share it; the invariants carry that case, and the mutations prove which oracle catches which break.

frequency.reason: a wrong reducer is the invariants' case by design, and the location-reducer mutation in the criteria proves an invariant catches it

outOfScope.summary: The player sees only what the page shows; a fact the bench does not render is one the player cannot reach, so a later block's panel must show what its goals need.

frequency.reason: every first-block fact (rooms, presence, holdings, ties, transit, offers, clock, schedule, history, received copies) is on the page, read in verify.txt's snapshot

outOfScope.summary: The calibrated T_ACT was set under the rule before this change (no pending precedence, reached by the done noul) and is kept, not re-swept, by the operator's condition; the calibration score records the old rule's runs.

Every snapshot the bench serves tries each verb by each person over the world's ids through the rules to find the pending states' resolutions; the cost grows with people, verbs and ids, bounded on the committed world and paid only while a schedule entry stands.

frequency.reason: a cost on every snapshot route read while a schedule entry stands, not a usage case: the committed world has three people, three items and two exits, so the tries are bounded by people times verbs times ids, and the engine's own apply path never pays it

outOfScope.summary: A pending state is seen only when it has a schedule entry; a later wait with no deadline would need one before the player could see it.

frequency.command: grep -n 'case "' src/engine/clock.ts (the actions that open a wait: physical.depart and exchange.offer, each scheduling its deadline)

walks.when: after merge, a fresh agent that is not RULE_AUTHOR and has read neither src/player/rule.ts nor corpus/goals/blind-1.json writes corpus/goals/blind-2.json (its own author, set blind-2, at least ten goals with typed expectations, at least one no-such-action and at least two whose end state is reached through an offer), and bun run src/player/score.ts --goals corpus/goals/blind-2.json --tick-minutes 10 runs on main with the real endpoints
walks.then: the score file reports reached on at least nine of every ten goals with loops and cost per goal, and the blind set, its score and its runs are committed under corpus/

walks.when: after merge, bun run src/player/main.ts "have Mux say something funny" --tick-minutes 10 --headed runs on main
walks.then: a browser window opens on the hosted bench, each loop's state text, questions, answers and action print as they happen, Mux's say appears in the history, and the run's four files are written under corpus/runs/

stakes: The driver calls the engine library (boot, act, step, events, received) and nothing lower; the player calls the page as a person does, through a real browser, and reads the history back through the bench's own routes; the definitions are never written.
The replay oracle composes the engine's own initialRows and applyPart over the log and compares state rows; it keeps no second copy of any fact and persists nothing.
The invariants read the registry, the schemas and the typed views; no subkind, field or code is listed a second time in the driver.

The player's candidates are read from the page each loop, one noul per candidate plus one goal-reached noul, recorded, in one Jev call; Jev never writes text, and a language model writes only the typed target and the words, each checked by code against what the page offers.
An instruction with no matching action ends in no-such-action; nothing invents a verb, an actor, an item or an exit the page does not show.
Every loop's request and answer are printed as they happen and recorded, and the browser can be watched.

The rule's thresholds are constants committed with the calibration goal set and its score before any blind set exists; a blind goal set carries an author other than the rule's recorded author, which score enforces by refusal, and is scored by expected end states after the merge.

Every player run is recorded as typed files under corpus/runs/<run-id>/ as it happens, with every question, answer, model call and cost, so a later block reads the corpus without the engine that produced it.
A refusal from either client stops the player naming its kind; the driver needs no model at all.
Every control on a strata page carries a clear label, held by a test that fails naming any that does not.

A pending state is a clock schedule entry, and its resolutions and their results are derived by running the engine's own rules and reducers on a copy of the rows, served by its own engine accessor through the bench's routes, never on the engine's apply path, and shown on the page; nothing about a pending state is stated a second time and no verb, subkind or part is named in deriving it.

The player's goal is a typed end state from the closed set (holder, location, said, no-such-action), checked by code against the bench; reached is that check, never a model's claim, and the done noul is recorded but decides nothing.

While a pending state whose resolution leaves the goal's end state stands, the next action is derived by code from that resolution and the clock is never stepped past its expiry; no action kind is named in that derivation.

T_DONE and T_ACT keep their calibrated values; nothing is re-tuned against a blind set, and the blind walk uses a fresh set written by an agent that has read neither the rule nor an earlier blind set.
